court: New York Supreme Court, Kings Trial Term
holding_summary: A person who hires desk room within a single undivided office from the tenants of that room has no independent tenancy or estate in the realty; when the landlord lawfully dispossesses the tenants without joining the desk-hirer, he cannot recover damages for being removed along with them, because his occupancy was legally no different from that of a person renting a room in a boarding or lodging house.

quotes.text: I do not think that the plaintiff had any tenancy or right apart from or outside of that of Reavy & Shook. He had no estate or interest in the real-estate.
His position was no better than that of one with a room in a boarding or lodging house.
He had to go out with them

notes: The court reaches its holding by analogy to the settled, unremarkable status of a lodger renting a room in a boarding/lodging house -- treated as having no estate in the realty (a license, not a tenancy). No actual boarding house is a party; the analogy is used to decide a desk-space-in-an-office dispute, so who_was_letting/duration are unclear on the facts actually before the court.
